title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
items.content_text: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has announced his departure, triggering a leadership search and a transition period where he will serve as a senior advisor. Despite beating Q1 expectations with a 15% revenue increase, the company's conservative full-year guidance triggered an 8% drop in after-hours stock trading.

items.title: HP Gives Profit Forecast Signaling Better Handle on Memory Costs
items.content_text: HP Inc. issued a fiscal profit forecast exceeding analyst consensus. The company aims to stabilize margins in a challenging PC and printer market by demonstrating improved control over volatile memory supply chain costs and structural efficiency.

items.title: A history professor says GPT-6.2 Astra solved a historical mystery in 22 minutes by identifying the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale (Mark Humphries/Generative History)
items.content_text: A history professor utilized GPT-6.2 Astra to identify the author of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale University within 22 minutes. The model successfully performed complex contextual reconstruction and archival cross-referencing, demonstrating a breakthrough in processing unstructured historical datasets.

items.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
items.content_text: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) of the U.S. Treasury has confirmed unauthorized access to a subset of its systems and initiated an investigation. FinCEN, responsible for anti-money laundering, has taken systems offline as a precaution while maintaining reporting channels via hotline.

items.title: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
items.content_text: Asian semiconductor stocks faced a rout following skepticism over ROI on AI capital expenditures and volatility in U.S. markets. Major suppliers including Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Samsung Electronics, and SK Hynix saw significant share price declines as AI accelerator demand confidence wavered.

items.title: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
items.content_text: Workday reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $2.82 and revenue of $2.705 billion, both exceeding analyst targets. However, the stock fell over 7% due to a conservative subscription revenue outlook. CEO Aneel Bhusri emphasized AI product growth and the acquisition of ConductorOne to strengthen agentic automation.

items.title: Utah prosecutors drop criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, one day after the company halted operations in the state (Marshall Cohen/CNN)
items.content_text: Utah Attorney General Derek Brown dropped criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and its founders after the company ceased operations in the state. This move signals an ongoing struggle between state anti-gambling laws and federal financial market regulation, with civil litigation still pending.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
items.content_text: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang just 11 days after his resignation, citing assurances from high-level U.S. government officials. However, intelligence experts warn that this move risks undermining national security enforcement, particularly as the company faces a criminal probe regarding alleged chip diversion to China.

items.title: WiseTech’s White Cleared in Human Trafficking Probe by Police
items.content_text: Australian police have concluded their investigation into Richard White, founder of WiseTech Global Ltd., following allegations of exploitation involving immigration status. The authorities decided to take no further action, effectively clearing the executive of the reported criminal allegations.

items.title: Trump leaves door open to Jensen Huang pardon — and urges him not to plead 5th to Congress next week
items.content_text: President Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, advising him to speak truthfully in upcoming congressional hearings rather than invoking the Fifth Amendment. Trump suggested that a presidential pardon remains an option, aiming to stabilize the firm amid intense congressional scrutiny over export controls and national security.

items.title: ‘The king is back!’ Huang’s return to Nvidia is greeted with relief in Asia.
items.content_text: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO triggered a strong rally in Asian markets, particularly in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea. Despite prior controversy surrounding his personal life and geopolitical ties, the regional tech ecosystem views his return as a critical signal for the continued stability of the global AI supply chain.

items.title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
items.content_text: Anthropic has launched the 'Install as app' beta for Claude on Mac and Windows, enabling users to transform Artifacts into standalone desktop applications with dedicated windows and system tray notifications. These apps can leverage Claude’s capabilities and local connectors under granular permission controls, facilitating deeper integration into professional workflows.

items.title: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand
items.content_text: Dell Technologies has raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year, fueled by record demand for AI infrastructure, with fiscal 2027 revenue now projected at $202 billion. Despite slower growth in the PC segment, Dell reported a record $132.3 billion backlog in AI servers, underscoring an accelerating refresh cycle for data center hardware.

items.title: Docs: Grubhub is on track for ~$6.4B in GTV and a $97M EBITDA loss in 2026, reflecting heavy marketing and operating costs; Wonder says it's not pursuing a sale (Valida Pau/The Information)
items.content_text: Marc Lore's Wonder is not pursuing a sale of Grubhub, Wonder says, after preliminary sales talks with Amazon and Walmart.

items.title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond
items.content_text: Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan was charged by federal prosecutors after installing hidden audio recorders in an executive conference room. OpenAI utilized internal AI tools to assist FBI investigations, confirming that no model weights or source code were compromised, and Alfozan has been released on bond.

items.title: A US jury finds Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud but acquits it of the most severe charge of criminal racketeering conspiracy (Associated Press)
items.content_text: A U.S. jury convicted Huawei Technologies on 10 out of 12 counts, including trade secret theft and bank fraud, while acquitting the company of the most serious 'racketeering conspiracy' charge. The case involves allegations of business dealings with sanctioned nations and providing false statements to banks; sentencing is scheduled for next September.

items.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
items.content_text: Anthropic now lets you install Claude Artifacts as Mac or Windows apps. The feature is in beta as of today and requires the latest version of Claude for macOS or Windows. You build an Artifact in chat and keep it in the dock without writing any code. The installed apps can use OS APIs, connectors, and Claude itself. That lets an app add menu bar items, create transparent windows, and send notifications, among other things. Examples include custom terminals, file managers, and video editors. Sev

items.title: Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
items.content_text: Jensen Huang apologized for past personal misconduct during his first all-hands meeting since returning as NVIDIA CEO. He explicitly denied allegations of political interference in his reinstatement and emphasized that NVIDIA’s unique decentralized leadership model eliminates the need for traditional succession planning.

items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas. During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely

items.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents
items.content_text: Anthropic announced that its Model Context Protocol (MCP) SDK has surpassed 700 million monthly downloads with over 10,000 connectors. New features, including background tasks, user elicitation, and upcoming file upload support, aim to enhance AI agent autonomy, while optimizing tool loading to reduce context usage by over 85% in multi-server environments.

items.title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
items.content_text: Director David Fincher's latest film has sparked controversy over uncanny, inconsistent visuals, leading to widespread speculation regarding the use of generative AI. While Netflix has not confirmed its usage, Fincher's recent public comments advocating for continuous creative iteration with AI have intensified industry debates over the intersection of professional filmmaking and synthetic media.

items.title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
items.content_text: Vas Narasimhan, CEO of Novartis and Anthropic board member, argued that complex human biology necessitates lengthy clinical trials, contradicting optimistic claims of curing major diseases within a decade. He projects that AI will reduce drug development time from 12 to 8 years and improve clinical success rates from 8% to 12% within the next ten years.

items.title: OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown urges promising students to drop out as AI enters a "very steep rate of progress"
items.content_text: Noam Brown, co-creator of OpenAI’s o1 reasoning model, stated that classical game theory fails in human-centric environments, necessitating AI models capable of ‘thinking before acting.’ He urged top-tier talent to prioritize AI research over formal education to capitalize on the current steep rate of technological progress.

items.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees in First All-Hands Since His Return
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the company’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. During his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the company’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two child

items.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
items.content_text: Music streaming platform Tidal announced it will ban fully AI-generated music effective December 9th, with plans to remove approximately 29 million tracks. Robert Andersen, the platform's music lead, stated that this drastic measure aims to protect artists and improve recommendations, citing that AI spam accounts for 43% of recent submissions and 96% of such tracks receive zero plays.

items.title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
items.content_text: Nvidia's board officially announced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director. The decision follows a series of internal discussions and interventions from senior levels of the U.S. government, concluding a period of turbulence triggered by controversies regarding his personal conduct and corporate governance.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.content_text: The New York Times photography leadership, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, has issued a directive prohibiting contributing photographers from using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (version 28.0.0 and later). The ban is designed to prevent the software's AI features from embedding C2PA metadata, which would falsely label authentic news photography as 'AI-generated' and threaten editorial integrity.

items.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
items.content_text: Anthropic researchers have developed 'Siren,' a honeypot testing system featuring 26 sandbox environments designed with intentional vulnerabilities. The system is intended to tempt AI agents into attempting to escape their constraints or perform unauthorized actions, allowing researchers to evaluate real-world safety risks and the models' capability to exploit zero-day vulnerabilities.

items.title: Anthropic researcher stands by his AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns up to "stupid things"in the rollout
items.content_text: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge stands by the mathematical validity of his AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, but he concedes he got several things wrong in how he released it. He says his claims about the work's length were meant as a joke and that he published the accompanying code without cleaning it up. items.title: Dozens of insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown their safety measures
items.content_text: Internal reports from OpenAI and Anthropic indicate that unreleased frontier models have grown so capable that many employees believe existing safety protocols are insufficient for oversight. Both organizations are currently engaged in internal debates over whether to halt the release of these high-capability systems entirely.
